caption: The drawing features a central stylized floral motif and two abstract, plant-like designs on either side, all rendered in muted shades of teal green, reddish-brown, and a muted salmon pink. The central flower has a rounded, segmented head with alternating teal and salmon ovals, edged by a geometric teal border. Emerging from the base of the flower are three elongated leaves, two in teal and one in reddish tones, each outlined with the contrasting color. The base of the stems is gathered together and wrapped by a circular, three-banded motif in alternating teal and salmon colors. Above the flower's head are three upward-extending stalks, two of which are reddish, each ending in rounded shapes. To the left of the central flower is an abstract, curving design resembling a leaf or tendril, featuring both teal and salmon colors. To the right is another abstract motif, possibly a stylized bird with a round teal body and salmon wing and beak, with a tail and leg shapes also created from teal and salmon curves. The background is a light beige color, and at the bottom center there is a typed label that reads: "SIDE ALTAR - San Luis Rey Mission INDEX OF AMERICAN DESIGN." Along the bottom edge, another small type label reads: "DECORATIVE ART OF SPANISH CALIFORNIA." In the bottom right, there is printed text: "W.P.A. ART PROJECT OF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA." There are two small black damaged areas at the top corners of the paper.
title: San Luis Rey Side Altar from the portfolio "Decorative Art of Spanish California"
